 Linn County auditor eyes more voting locations as early voting grows 
 By Brian Tabick Published : Nov. 5, 2026 at 9:06 PM CST | Updated : 4 hours ago Share Add Us On Google Add as a preferred source on Google CEDAR RAPIDS, Iowa (KCRG) - Linn County Auditor Todd Taylor said he is looking to add more voting locations in future elections after nearly 500,000 Iowans voted absentee in the 2026 midterm election.
 Of those absentee voters, 70% voted in person rather than by mail.
 Early voting in Linn County
 Lines to vote in the 2026 midterm election were packed across eastern Iowa. Voters gave their own reasons for voting early.
 “I couldn’t guarantee that I was going to make it to the opening times,” Cooper Wadle said.
 “I don’t know if my vote will make a difference. I hope it does,” Dave Miller said.
 Linn County had more than 40,000 early voters. Taylor said 27,000 of them voted in person at Lindale Mall or at the auditor’s office. That number does not include five short-term locations in Cedar Rapids and Marion.
 Looking ahead to 2028
 Taylor said the number of early voters has him thinking about future elections.
 “I want to make sure that people are using the options that we give them, and at the end of the day, I am thinking about the presidential election in 2028. We’ll have a little bit larger turnout, I would think,” Taylor said.
 Secretary of State Paul Pate said the Linn County numbers reflect what was seen statewide. Nearly half a million people voted early, and 70% of them voted in person.
 Plans for a west side location
 Taylor said he wants to add a new satellite location on the west side of Cedar Rapids, similar to the Lindale Mall site.
 “We can accommodate on average about 1,000 people a day out there, and we did that for 20 days,” Taylor said.
 Taylor said a new location would give more people an option to make their voices heard, especially in an election where more people are likely to vote early.
 “I know that voting is super important, and I know that it’s a privilege to be able to vote,” Kyle Vedepo said.
 How to request a satellite location
 Taylor said people need to file a petition with the county to add a satellite voting location. The petition requires proper paperwork and 100 signatures submitted to the auditor’s office ahead of the next election.
